violations.reason: The image's alt text is 'DSC_0481.JPG', which is a raw camera filename rather than a meaningful description. The image depicts a protest/demonstration scene with signs reading 'FAIR FARES', 'NO HIKE', 'RIDERS', and 'UNITE', but this informative content is not conveyed to assistive technology. A filename does not provide an equivalent text alternative, violating SC 1.1.1.
violations.recommendation: Replace the filename with a meaningful text alternative that conveys the image's content and purpose, e.g. alt="Protesters holding signs reading 'Fair Fares', 'No Hike', 'Riders Unite' in front of a building." If the image is purely decorative, use alt="".

gena11y.summary: One image uses the camera filename 'DSC_0481.JPG' as its alt text, which is not a meaningful text alternative for its informative protest-scene content, violating SC 1.1.1.

violations.reason:
The weekly menu is genuinely tabular data (rows = days Monday–Friday, columns = Breakfast/Lunch/Snack) but it is rendered as plain text inside a single

element with columns aligned only by whitespace/spaces. The row/column relationships and the header cells (Breakfast, Lunch, Snack) are conveyed visually through spacing alone and are not programmatically determinable. Assistive technology reads it as one run-on paragraph, so the association between a day, a meal type, and a menu item is lost — a WCAG 1.3.1 failure (whitespace 'table' in plain text, missing /
/scope).
violations.recommendation: Replace the whitespace-formatted paragraph with a real <table>. Use a <caption> (or aria-labelledby to the h2), a <thead> row of <th scope="col"> for Breakfast/Lunch/Snack, and for each day a <th scope="row"> with the weekday plus <td> cells for the meals so the data relationships are programmatically exposed.

The screenshot shows a 'Riverside Metro' network map with three colored route lines (green, red, blue). Per the tested rules, there are no text links that rely on color alone (no hyperlink styling present) and no form fields (required/error) at all. The transit lines, while color-coded, are also differentiated by distinct spatial position (top/middle/bottom) and named endpoint stations (West End–Airport, Union Square, Vale–Fairgrounds), so color is not the sole means of distinguishing routes. No clear 1.4.1 link/form violation is present.

At 400% zoom (1280×1024, ~320 CSS px effective width) the page reflows correctly into a single column: the header/nav, the 'Trending This Week' heading, and the intro paragraph all wrap and stack vertically with no page-level horizontal scrollbar and no clipped or lost content. The 'Top sellers' product row is a self-contained horizontal-scroll carousel (explicitly 'Swipe the row to browse'), whose contained one-dimensional scrolling is an intentional widget pattern and does not force two-dimensional scrolling of the page itself. Neither stated failure (content disappearing, or two-dimensional page scrolling to read content) is evidenced in the reflowed view.

Assuming the default white card background, all dark rgb(26,26,26) text achieves ~17:1 contrast (well above 4.5:1). The lightest text, rgb(138,138,138) at 24px (=18pt, large text), reaches ~3.45:1 which meets the 3:1 large-text threshold, so no clear WCAG 1.4.3 violation is present.

The visible content is a single personal letter — one continuous section of prose with a clear descriptive heading ('A Letter Home — Pvt. Edwin Marsden to his mother, June 1944'). A letter is a single narrative unit; the location/date block and 'Dear Mother,' salutation are conventional letter parts, not distinct sections that each require their own heading. No clear SC 2.4.10 violation is evident.

violations.reason: The page title is 'Untitled Document', a generic default placeholder generated by authoring tools. It does not describe the page's topic or purpose, which is an investor relations quarterly results report ('Northwind Trading Posts Record Q3 Revenue, Driven by Logistics Segment'). WCAG 2.4.2 requires the title to describe the page's topic or purpose so users can identify the page without reading its content.
violations.recommendation: Replace the placeholder with a descriptive title, e.g., '<title>Northwind Trading Posts Record Q3 Revenue, Driven by Logistics Segment | Investor Relations</title>'.

gena11y.summary: The page has a non-empty title, but it is the generic placeholder 'Untitled Document' which fails to describe the page's actual content (Northwind Trading's Q3 revenue report), violating SC 2.4.2.

violations.reason:
The link's accessible name 'Read the full document' is generic and does not describe its destination. The surrounding context (a preceding

that merely repeats 'Read the full document') adds no clarifying information about what document is being linked. Furthermore, this link has an identical name to the other 'Read the full document' link on the page yet points to a different destination (fee-schedule-2025.pdf vs bus-routes-fall.pdf), so identically-named links serve non-equivalent purposes.
violations.recommendation: Give the link descriptive text such as 'Read the full 2025 fee schedule (PDF)', or provide clarifying context in the same paragraph/list item. Ensure links with the same visible text lead to the same or an equivalent destination.
